questions.question: What roles do title and meta description play in search results?
questions.answer: title is the strongest on-page signal and the default result heading; keep it unique and about 50–60 characters. meta description is a 120–160 character snippet suggestion — search engines may rewrite it from page content.

questions.question: When and why do you use a canonical link?
questions.answer: When the same content is reachable at multiple URLs (params, trailing slash, http/https), canonical names the preferred URL so search engines consolidate ranking signals. It is a hint, not a redirect.

questions.question: What is the difference between Open Graph and Twitter card tags?
questions.answer: Open Graph (og:*) controls previews on Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack, and others and uses property attributes. Twitter/X uses twitter:* tags and falls back to Open Graph; twitter:card selects the layout.

questions.question: What is JSON-LD and what rule must it follow?
questions.answer: JSON-LD is structured data in a script type=application/ld+json block describing the page (Article, Person, FAQ, Product) for rich results. It must match visible page content; marking up absent ratings/FAQs is spam.

questions.question: Write the SEO head for Kakade's forms article with title, description, canonical, and robots.
questions.answer:
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>HTML Forms for Interviews — Kakade.dev</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Labels, validation, GET vs POST, and accessible form controls." />
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://kakade.dev/html/forms" />
  <meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />
</head>

questions.question: Add Open Graph and Twitter card metadata for the same article.
questions.answer:
<meta property="og:title" content="HTML Forms for Interviews" />
<meta property="og:description" content="Labels, validation, and accessible controls." />
<meta property="og:image" content="https://kakade.dev/img/forms-cover.png" />
<meta property="og:url" content="https://kakade.dev/html/forms" />
<meta property="og:type" content="article" />

<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
<meta name="twitter:title" content="HTML Forms for Interviews" />

questions.question: Why is JavaScript-only navigation like <div onclick="location.href='...'"> bad for SEO?
questions.answer: Crawlers rely on real href values to discover and follow links. A div with a click handler exposes no link target, so pages may never be crawled and users lose middle-click/open-in-new-tab behavior.

questions.question: Should you stuff keywords into alt text and headings?
questions.answer: No. Alt should describe the image and headings should structure the content. Keyword stuffing is a spam signal, degrades screen-reader experience, and search engines understand topical relevance without repetition.
